title: Overtime as a cost, not a rule

blocks.text: A window-cleaning company runs two crews from one yard. Overtime is allowed but costly, and the crews have different finish times (one crew works a short day). Rather than refuse a plan that brings a crew back late, the planner wants each late minute to cost money, so the solver trades overtime against travel. `overtime.py` builds the routes and a "Time" dimension whose cumul at a crew's end is the minute it is back at the yard. Write `add_overtime_cost(routing, time_dim, finish_by, cost_per_minute)`.
In the lesson's notation, with $`e_v`$ crew $`v`$'s end index and $`F_v`$ its finish time, the objective becomes

with $`\gamma`$ the cost per minute. No plan is refused for lateness. Before you code, say which index carries a crew's return time and which call adds a term of the form $`\gamma \max(0, \text{cumul} - F)`$.
The tests read the objective of hand-built plans, so any correct formulation passes. Two lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from ortools.constraint_solver import pywrapcp


def add_overtime_cost(routing, time_dim, finish_by: list[int], cost_per_minute: int) -> None:
    """Each crew v should be back by finish_by[v]; every minute later costs cost_per_minute."""
    for vehicle, bound in enumerate(finish_by):
        time_dim.SetCumulVarSoftUpperBound(routing.End(vehicle), bound, cost_per_minute)


def build(travel: list[list[int]], service: list[int], finish_by: list[int], cost_per_minute: int):
    """Given: one route per crew from the depot (node 0), priced in travel minutes, with a Time
    dimension that starts every crew at 0 and adds the work at each stop to the travel."""
    manager = pywrapcp.RoutingIndexManager(len(travel), len(finish_by), 0)
    routing = pywrapcp.RoutingModel(manager)

    def drive(from_index, to_index):
        return travel[manager.IndexToNode(from_index)][manager.IndexToNode(to_index)]

    def busy(from_index, to_index):
        here = manager.IndexToNode(from_index)
        return service[here] + travel[here][manager.IndexToNode(to_index)]

    routing.SetArcCostEvaluatorOfAllVehicles(routing.RegisterTransitCallback(drive))
    routing.AddDimension(routing.RegisterTransitCallback(busy), 0, 24 * 60, True, "Time")
    add_overtime_cost(routing, routing.GetDimensionOrDie("Time"), finish_by, cost_per_minute)
    return manager, routing


if __name__ == "__main__":
    manager, routing = build([[0, 5, 9], [5, 0, 6], [9, 6, 0]], [0, 20, 20], [40, 40], 3)
    plan = routing.ReadAssignmentFromRoutes([[1, 2], []], True)
    print(plan.ObjectiveValue() if plan else None)

cases.says: a crew back on time adds nothing to the objective, and a crew back late adds the cost per minute times the minutes late
when two crews are back late, each one's lateness is charged
a crew with a later finish time is not charged for coming back after another crew's finish time

origin.section: A Soft Upper Bound Charges for Lateness Instead of Forbidding It

concepts: a soft upper bound on a cumul adds a cost per unit above the bound instead of forbidding it
